meta.note: Greek records are verified against the Evelyn-White (1914) Theogony. Norse and Egyptian records are still seeds (verified=false, no locators). roles and domains are editorial tags, not individually cited.

records.name: Typhon

sources.claim: Hundred-headed child of Earth and Tartarus, struck down by Zeus
Said to be the mate of Echidna
sources.note: The Theogony uses Typhaon here and Typhoeus at l. 821; this database treats them as one figure (editorial identification).

sources.claim: Called Typhaon: born to Hera without Zeus and fostered by a dragoness
sources.note: Differs from the Theogony (ll. 820-868), where Earth bears Typhoeus.

records.summary: In the Theogony a hundred-headed child of Earth and Tartarus, struck down by Zeus, and the mate of Echidna. In the Hymn to Apollo he is called Typhaon and is instead born to Hera without Zeus and fostered by a dragoness.

records.name: Echidna

sources.claim: Half nymph, half snake, living in a cave in Arima
Mother of Orthus, Cerberus, the Hydra, the Chimaera, the Sphinx and the Nemean lion

records.summary: A half-nymph, half-snake who lives in a cave in Arima. Typhon is said to be her mate, and she is the mother of Orthus, Cerberus, the Hydra, the Chimaera, the Sphinx and the Nemean lion.

records.name: Lernaean Hydra

sources.claim: Raised by Hera; destroyed by Heracles and Iolaus with Athena's help
Nine-headed beast bred in the swamp of Lerna, with one immortal head; killed by Heracles and Iolaus

records.summary: A nine-headed beast bred in the swamp of Lerna, with one immortal head. The Theogony says Hera raised her out of anger at Heracles. Heracles and Iolaus destroy her, with Athena's help according to the Theogony.

records.name: Cerberus

sources.claim: Fifty-headed hound of Hades
A hound guards the halls of Hades and keeps the dead in
sources.note: Cerberus is not named in this passage.

records.summary: The fifty-headed hound of Hades. Another passage describes a hound that guards the halls of Hades and keeps the dead in, though it does not name him.

records.name: Medusa

sources.claim: The mortal Gorgon; Perseus beheads her, and Pegasus and Chrysaor spring from her
The only mortal Gorgon; beheaded by Perseus, and Pegasus and Chrysaor spring from her, begotten by Poseidon

records.summary: The only mortal Gorgon. Perseus beheads her, and Pegasus and Chrysaor spring from her; Apollodorus says Poseidon was their father.

records.name: Pegasus

sources.claim: Springs from Medusa when Perseus cuts off her head; flies to the gods and lives in Zeus's house, bringing him thunder and lightning
Slays the Chimaera with Bellerophon
Begotten, with Chrysaor, by Poseidon

records.summary: A winged horse who springs from Medusa when Perseus cuts off her head; Apollodorus says Poseidon was his father. He flies to the gods, lives in the house of Zeus and brings him thunder and lightning. With Bellerophon he slays the Chimaera.

records.name: Chrysaor

sources.claim: Springs from Medusa when Perseus cuts off her head; joined to Callirrhoe, he fathers three-headed Geryon
Father, by the Oceanid Callirrhoe, of Geryon
Begotten, with Pegasus, by Poseidon

records.summary: He springs from Medusa when Perseus cuts off her head, and Apollodorus says Poseidon was his father. With the Oceanid Callirrhoe he fathers three-headed Geryon.

records.name: Geryon

sources.claim: Three-headed child of Chrysaor; Heracles kills him in Erythea for his oxen
The strongest of men; killed by Heracles for his shambling oxen

records.summary: A three-headed son of Chrysaor and Callirrhoe, called the strongest of men. Heracles kills him in Erythea for his oxen.

records.name: Orthus

sources.claim: The hound of Geryon, killed by Heracles
The first offspring of Echidna and Typhaon; later, with Echidna, father of the Sphinx and the Nemean lion

records.summary: The hound of Geryon, killed by Heracles. He is the first offspring of Echidna and Typhaon, and with Echidna he later fathers the Sphinx and the Nemean lion.

records.name: The Chimaera

sources.claim: A fire-breathing monster with a lion's head, a dragon's hindpart and a goat's middle, killed by Pegasus and Bellerophon

records.summary: A fire-breathing monster with a lion's head, a goat's middle and a dragon's tail, killed by Pegasus and Bellerophon.

records.name: The Sphinx

sources.claim: Born to Echidna by Orthus; destroys the Cadmeans

records.summary: A deadly monster born to Echidna by Orthus, who destroys the Cadmeans.

records.name: The Nemean Lion

sources.claim: Born to Echidna by Orthus; raised by Hera to plague the hills of Nemea; overcome by Heracles
The first beast Heracles faces in the labours set by Eurystheus

records.summary: A lion born to Echidna by Orthus, raised by Hera to plague the hills of Nemea. Heracles overcomes it, and Apollodorus makes it the first of his labours.

records.name: The Cyclopes

sources.claim: Three one-eyed sons of Earth and Heaven, Brontes, Steropes and Arges, who gave Zeus the thunder and made the thunderbolt

records.summary: Three one-eyed sons of Earth and Heaven, Brontes, Steropes and Arges, who gave Zeus thunder and made his thunderbolt.

records.name: The Hundred-Handers

sources.claim: Cottus, Briareos and Gyes, sons of Earth and Heaven with a hundred arms and fifty heads each, hidden away by their father
Freed from their bonds under the earth on Earth's advice; Zeus feeds them nectar and they promise to fight the Titans
Bury the Titans under rocks and become their warders in Tartarus
Cottus and Gyes live on the foundations of Ocean; Poseidon makes Briareos his son-in-law

records.summary: Cottus, Briareos and Gyes, sons of Earth and Heaven, each with a hundred arms and fifty heads. Their father hides them away, and Zeus frees them to fight the Titans, whom they bury under rocks and then guard. Poseidon makes Briareos his son-in-law.
